articles.title: India's First AI -Powered Locomotive Developed at Patiala - Drishti IAS
articles.content: Punjab Prev Next India’s First AI-Powered Locomotive Developed at Patiala 22 Sep 2026 2 min read Why in News? Patiala Locomotive Works (PLW) has developed India’s first AI-powered locomotive equipped with an Artificial Intelligence-based Overhead Equipment (OHE) monitoring system . Key Points First of its Kind: PLW has developed the country’s first AI-powered rail engine for railway safety monitoring. The locomotive is equipped with an AI-based Overhead Equipment (OHE) monitoring system that continuously monitors overhead power lines and tracks during the journey. The system has been installed on locomotive number 39642 . Inauguration: The AI-powered locomotive was flagged off by Neelam Devi , a senior woman employee and technician of PLW, in the presence of S. K. Srivastava , Principal Chief Administrative Officer of PLW. Predictive Detection: The AI system can identify potential faults in advance and alert the maintenance team before a major problem occurs. The system can detect electrical wiring sparks, loose wires and damaged components associated with the OHE and moving train. Pilot Project: The Railways has commissioned four such engines as part of a pilot project. The AI-powered locomotive was developed over a period of one year . Locomotive Category: The passenger electric locomotive belongs to the WP-7 category . Technology: The system integrates sensors, live monitoring, data analysis and predictive maintenance. articles.title: M1xchange becomes India's first TReDS platform to go live with CGTMSE guarantee cover ...
articles.content: The Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE), set up to facilitate credit flow to eligible Micro and Small Enterprises through credit guarantee support, is extending its guaranteed framework to receivables financing through TReDS. Collaboration across the ecosystem: The Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MoMSME), CGTMSE and M1xchange have collaborated to operationalise the guaranteed mechanism for eligible MSE receivables financed through TReDS. First CGTMSE-backed TReDS transaction: M1xchange has successfully completed the first transaction on its TReDS platform backed by CGTMSE guarantee cover, bringing the benefits of credit guarantee support into the TReDS financing framework. Wider liquidity access for MSMEs: By strengthening the financing proposition for eligible receivables on TReDS, the initiative can support greater access to timely working capital for MSME sellers. Added risk support for financiers: The mechanism provides participating financiers with access to applicable CGTMSE guarantee support for eligible receivables, supporting greater participation in MSE financing. CGTMSE is integrated with M1xchange’s TReDS platform via APIs, digitizing the entire guaranteed journey for financiers. Financiers can check invoice eligibility and apply for CGTMSE cover in real time on the platform. This triggers automatic guarantee fee calculation based on invoice value, financier type and tenor, fee debit on a T+1 basis, and automatic generation of the cover note and corresponding invoice. Sundeep Mohindru, Founder & Promoter, M1xchange, “Integrating CGTMSE with M1xchange brings a significant change to the way credit risk can be managed in receivables financing. By making the guarantee journey digital and transaction-level, we are enabling financiers to assess and access eligible guarantee cover seamlessly. This will enable flow of receivable financing to deep tiers of Micro and Small enterprises. We see it as a significant step in strengthening India’s MSME supply chains at a time when they need it most.” The development follows the Union Budget 2026 announcement on credit guarantee support for TReDS transactions and the RBI’s 2026 TReDS framework, which permits financiers to avail guarantee cover from eligible Government-established credit guarantee trusts. Shri Manish Sinha, Chief Executive Officer, CGTMSE, said, “TReDS has played a significant role in improving working capital access for MSMEs. The integration of CGTMSE’s guarantee mechanism with a digital TReDS platform can make the process more seamless for financiers while supporting greater participation in eligible MSME receivables financing. We see this as an important step towards strengthening the credit ecosystem for the MSME sector.” Dr. Rajneesh, IAS, Additional Secretary & Development Commissioner, Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MoMSME), said, “Extending CGTMSE-backed guarantee cover to TReDS receivables is an important step in translating the Union Budget’s MSME support measures into on-ground impact, further strengthening the financing ecosystem for MSMEs by improving access to timely and formal sources of credit.” For corporates and large buyers, the digital infrastructure can support supplier financing programmes at scale. This will benefit M1xchange’s ecosystem, comprising 81+ banks, 15,000+ corporates and 1,10,000+ MSMEs, by enabling greater access to guarantee-backed receivables financing.

articles.title: CMF and Optiemus Expand Partnership to Build India's First End-to-End Smartphone R&D Capability
articles.content: Updated 22 September 2026 at 14:26 IST The expanded partnership will see Optiemus join CMF's upcoming Series A round, with the brand moving towards majority Indian ownership and developing smartphone design, engineering and software capabilities in India. Digital Desk Tech News 3 min read Follow : Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw, (Left), Carl Pei, CEO of Nothing (Centre), Ashok Gupta, Executive Chairman of Optiemus (Right) | Image: ANI CMF by Nothing and Optiemus Group have expanded their partnership to build what the companies describe as India's first full-stack, end-to-end smartphone research and development capability. As part of the expanded partnership, Optiemus will join Nothing's upcoming Series A investment round for CMF, putting the brand on a path towards majority Indian ownership. The development builds on the manufacturing joint venture announced by Nothing and Optiemus in September 2025, which established India as a production hub for Nothing and CMF products. The companies now plan to bring manufacturing, ownership and R&D under a single Indian entity associated with CMF. The stated objective is to move beyond assembling smartphones in India and develop the technology behind them locally. CMF says its investment in local R&D and engineering will help expand India's role in the smartphone value chain from manufacturing to technology development and global exports. Under the expanded partnership, CMF plans to develop capabilities across six areas: industrial design, mechanical engineering, camera engineering, software engineering, connectivity engineering and component engineering. Advertisement Industrial design will cover the phone's form, materials and overall design, while mechanical engineering will focus on areas such as structural design, thermal systems and hardware architecture. Camera engineering will involve camera systems, sensors and image processing, while software engineering will cover the operating system and software powering the devices. The planned connectivity engineering function will focus on antennas, radio systems and network performance. CMF also plans to work directly with component suppliers through its component engineering capabilities to develop, test and optimise components used in its products. Advertisement A key part of the initiative is intellectual property. CMF says the IP generated through these activities will be held locally, with smartphones intended to be designed and engineered in India rather than simply assembled in the country. The companies also point to the concentration of smartphone engineering and component ecosystems in China as a reference for the opportunity they see in India. According to the release, CMF wants to develop a similar demand-driven ecosystem locally, connecting engineering talent, component suppliers, local intellectual property and product development. CMF was founded by Nothing in 2023 and currently operates in more than 40 countries. The company claims it sold millions of units globally and recorded 83 per cent year-on-year volume growth in India in 2025, citing Counterpoint Research's Q4 2025 India Smartphone Shipment Tracker. For Optiemus, the partnership builds on its existing electronics manufacturing operations in India. The publicly listed company operates across mobile devices, IT hardware, telecom equipment, hearables and wearables, precision cover glass and defence-grade unmanned systems, with five manufacturing units across India. articles.title: India's First Broadband Chip Moves Towards Commercialisation
articles.content: Exclusive Semicon India’s First Broadband Chip Moves Towards Commercialisation By Saba Aafreen Share Facebook X Pinterest WhatsApp Linkedin Telegram Aheesa presents Vihaan-I Semicon chip to Union Minister Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw at Semicon India 2026 September 22, 2026 What does India’s first indigenous broadband chip bring to the country’s networking ecosystem? Vihaan-I has completed first-pass silicon and is now moving towards commercialisation. Aheesa Digital Innovations has unveiled Vihaan-I, an indigenously designed broadband networking chip, at SEMICON India 2026 in the presence of Union Minister for Electronics and IT – Ashwini Vaishnaw . The (design linked incentive) DLI scheme-backed fabless semiconductor company is targeting early 2027 for commercialisation of the chip. Vihaan-I is designed for broadband and fibre networking equipment used in homes and offices. It brings core networking functions onto a single system-on-chip (SoC), built on the open-standard reduced instruction set computing-five (RISC-V) architecture and powered by the indigenous VEGA processor developed by the Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC). Aheesa said the chip was designed in India by its engineering team, apart from standard IP such as Wi-Fi. In an exclusive interaction with EFY , Saket Singh , director and chief growth officer, Aheesa Digital Innovations, said the company’s immediate focus is on getting Vihaan-I into the hands of broadband and telecom equipment makers. Aheesa has signed a packaging memorandum of understanding (MoU) with Optilink Networks covering product development from prototyping through packaging and joint development of broadband customer equipment. It has also signed a distribution partnership with The Zigma Technologies India. The company completed Vihaan-I’s tape-out on January 26, 2026, and received the silicon by the end of July. Testing subsequently resulted in first-pass silicon success on August 15, according to Aheesa. The company is now moving from silicon validation towards production readiness and commercial deployment. The unveiling was also acknowledged amongst the Made-in-India semiconductor developments by the minister. The recognition comes as Aheesa begins building the ecosystem required to take the chip into commercial broadband equipment. Vihaan-I, Aheesa’s indigenously designed broadband networking chip Singh said the company is currently focused on India and South Asia for deployment, while also exploring licensing opportunities in the UK and US. Aheesa plans to remain fabless, with manufacturing handled through external foundry partners. The company said it is currently using United Microelectronics Corporation (UMC) and would explore Indian fabs as domestic manufacturing capacity becomes available. Vihaan-I is also intended to form the foundation for a broader networking semiconductor roadmap. Singh said the company plans to build on the platform beyond its current 1G capability, with future development spanning broadband, telecom and cybersecurity applications. So, what will it take to move Vihaan-I from successful silicon to commercial deployment? Which broadband equipment makers and manufacturing partners are needed to take the chip into products, and how does the company plan to scale the platform beyond its first version? articles.title: Microsoft Launches Fourth Cloud Region In Hyderabad - Telangana Today
articles.content: NRI View Point cartoon My Space Reviews Education Today Property Lifestyle Home | Hyderabad | Microsoft Launches Fourth Cloud Region In Hyderabad Microsoft Launches Fourth Cloud Region In Hyderabad Microsoft has launched its fourth cloud region in India, India South Central, in Hyderabad as part of its $20.5-billion investment commitment. The new region will support advanced AI workloads, strengthen Microsoft's cloud infrastructure, and feature sustainable zero-water cooling technology. By Telangana Today Published Date - 22 September 2026, 01:10 PM Hyderabad: Microsoft has launched its fourth cloud region in India in Hyderabad, expanding its infrastructure for cloud and artificial intelligence workloads. Called India South Central, the new datacentre region is being positioned as a strategic hub for Asia and the Global South. The Hyderabad region is part of Microsoft’s $20.5-billion investment commitment in India and features a three-zone architecture designed to provide resilience and support future expansion. The region is already live, with additional Azure and AI services expected to be introduced over the coming months. Puneet Chandok, President, Microsoft India and South Asia, said in a press release, “India South Central is our fourth cloud region in the country, built for advanced AI workloads and a strategic hub for Asia and the Global South.” As mentioned in the press release, organisations including Adani Group, Bajaj Finserv, HDFC Bank and PB Pay have already signed up for the new region. One of the key features of the Hyderabad facility is its cooling system. Microsoft said the India South Central region operates with a zero-water cooling, using high-efficiency mechanical systems that do not use water for cooling. The approach is part of the company’s broader sustainability goals, including its target of becoming carbon negative, water positive and zero waste by 2030. The new region also expands Microsoft’s sovereign public cloud capabilities in India, offering local capacity, data residency options, Availability Zones and governance features for eligible workloads. As noted in the press release, the infrastructure is designed to help organisations address applicable security, compliance and data protection requirements. Microsoft is also working on regional connectivity through the planned 3,600-km India-Southeast Asia (I-2SEA) submarine cable system, which will connect India with Malaysia and Singapore. The cable will have landing points at Machilipatnam and South Chennai and is targeted to be ready for service in 2029. In Telangana, Microsoft’s Data Center Academy is also being delivered in collaboration with Young India Skills University and the Government of Telangana. The 600-hour programme is aimed at preparing students for careers in datacenter operations and infrastructure management. The company said more than 10 million Indians have already been equipped with AI skills, towards its target of skilling 20 million people by 2030. articles.title: Safdarjung Hospital hosts India's first robotic cardiac surgery workshop - The News Mill
articles.content: Vardhman Mahavir Medical College (VMMC) and Safdarjung Hospital conducted India’s first workshop dedicated solely to robotic cardiac surgery, uniting cardiac surgeons for live surgical demonstrations and hands-on training in advanced robotic techniques. The two-day Asia Pacific Robotic Cardiac Workshop: Intracardiac – Part 1 was organised by the Department of Cardiothoracic and Vascular Surgery (CTVS) at Safdarjung Hospital on September 17 and 18. ADVERTISEMENT Stay connected Make The News Mill your preferred source See more TNM stories when you search for news on Google. Add TNM on Google Led by Professor Anubhav Gupta, Director Professor and Head of the CTVS department, the workshop aimed to enhance training and provide practical exposure in robotic cardiac surgery. During the event, the CTVS team successfully performed two live robotic cardiac surgeries, showcasing robotic-assisted, minimally invasive surgical techniques. Additionally, over seven hours of hands-on simulation sessions were held to train cardiac surgeons in robotic surgical procedures. ADVERTISEMENT The workshop emphasised key aspects of robotic intracardiac surgery and included participation from senior cardiac surgeons nationwide. It focused on advanced surgical training, simulation, and practical experience in robotic cardiac procedures. VMMC and Safdarjung Hospital stated that the initiative reflects their commitment to advanced patient care, medical education, research, and technological innovation in specialised surgical fields. The workshop also underscores efforts to promote robotic cardiac surgery and improve access to advanced healthcare practices within the public sector. The event was attended by guest faculty and medical professionals including Dr Manoj Durairaj, former president of the Indian Association of Cardiovascular-Thoracic Surgeons (IACTS); Dr Vinitha Nair, Executive Member, IACTS; Dr Vijay Grover of Atal Bihari Vajpayee Institute of Medical Sciences (ABVIMS), New Delhi; Dr Nitin Rajput of Medanta, Gurugram; and Dr Devagourou, Head of the Department of CTVS at AIIMS, New Delhi. articles.title: India Sends Largest Contingent to WorldSkills Shanghai 2026 - GKToday
articles.content: Home India Sends Largest Contingent to WorldSkills Shanghai 2026 India Sends Largest Contingent to WorldSkills Shanghai 2026 September 22, 2026 Current Affairs Today - Latest Current Affairs - 2026-2027 India has sent its largest-ever contingent of 70 skilled competitors to the 48th WorldSkills Competition in Shanghai, China, scheduled from 22 to 27 September 2026. The Indian team will compete in 63 of the 64 skill categories at the National Exhibition and Convention Centre in Shanghai. WorldSkills Competition The WorldSkills Competition is an international skills event for young professionals and trainees. It is organised in different skill trades and technologies, including construction, manufacturing, information technology, and service sectors. India’s Participation in 2026 India will make its debut in 11 skill categories at the 2026 edition. These categories include Dental Prosthetics, Digital Interactive Media Design, Intelligent Security Technology, Landscape Gardening, Optoelectronic Technology, Retail Sales, Unmanned Aerial Systems, Industrial Mechanics, Software Testing, Heavy Vehicle Technology, and Aircraft Maintenance. The contingent includes participants from 16 states. Karnataka, Odisha, and Tamil Nadu have the largest representation in the team. Institutional Support and Preparation The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship and the National Skill Development Corporation are leading India’s participation and preparation for the competition. A send-off ceremony for the contingent was held in New Delhi on 15 September 2026, and Minister of State Jayant Chaudhary addressed the team. Jindal Steel has joined as an official sponsor for India’s participation in WorldSkills Shanghai 2026. Important Facts for Exams WorldSkills Competition is held for young skilled professionals across multiple vocational trades and technologies. Shanghai will host the 48th WorldSkills Competition at the National Exhibition and Convention Centre. India will compete in 63 out of 64 skill categories in the 2026 edition. India’s global skills ranking improved from 29th in 2015 to 13th in 2024. India’s Recent Performance in Skill Events India secured 8th rank at WorldSkills Asia 2025. The country also won five medals at the Taipei Capital Cup 2026. articles.title: India's first blue bond set for launch next week, official says
articles.content: Articles 1 min read India's first blue bond set for launch next week, official says India's first maritime lender, Sagarmala Finance Corporation, plans to raise funds through the country's maiden blue bond on September 28, its top Reuters Published On Sep 22, 2026 at 10:32 AM IST Select ETBFSI as Preferred Choice on Google Copy Link Share on WhatsApp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook By Khushi Malhotra MUMBAI, Sept 22 - India's first maritime lender, Sagarmala Finance Corporation , plans to raise funds through the country's maiden blue bond on September 28, its top executive said. The lender aims to raise 6 billion rupees ($62.62 million), including a greenshoe option of 5 billion rupees, through the sale of 10-year bonds, a provisional term sheet showed. Blue bonds are a debt instrument used to finance sustainable water and marine projects, including clean water, recycling, shipping, sustainable fishing, ocean energy and mapping. The proceeds will be used for maritime sector lending, greenfield port projects, funding coastal road network and more, Managing Director L.V.S. Sudhakar Babu told Reuters late on Monday, adding that the funds will be used within the current financial year. Advt SBI Capital markets is the arranger for the issue, rated AA+ by Icra and Care. The company will invite coupon and commitment bids from investors on Monday, Babu said. The lender has also reached out to large insurance and provident fund players to invest in this issue. Vadodara Municipal Corporation, an urban local body from the state of Gujarat, is also planning to raise around two billion rupees through the sale of blue bonds soon, Reuters reported earlier. articles.title: NIT Srinagar Set To Become India's First NIT With Dedicated Astronomy Observatory ...
articles.content: NIT Srinagar Set To Become India’s First NIT With Dedicated Astronomy Observatory Featuring High-Performance 14-Inch Telescope NIT-Srinagar will inaugurate the Observatory for Astronomy and Astrophysics, becoming the first NIT with a dedicated campus observatory. Equipped with a 14-inch Celestron C14 EdgeHD telescope, the facility will support astrophotography, research, student training and astronomy outreach. Add FPJ As a Trusted Source PTI Updated: Tuesday, September 22, 2026, 09:52 AM IST NIT Srinagar Set To Become India’s First NIT With Dedicated Astronomy Observatory Featuring High-Performance 14-Inch Telescope | Srinagar: The National Institute of Technology (NIT) here is set to become the country's first NIT to have a dedicated campus-based observatory equipped with a high-performance 14-inch aplanatic Schmidt-Cassegrain telescope, officials said on Monday. The telescope provides aberration-free flat-field images for advanced astrophotography and planetary observation. The Observatory for Astronomy and Astrophysics (NSOAA) will be inaugurated on Tuesday, marking a significant milestone in science education and research, they said. "The facility will bring advanced observational astronomy to the campus and create a new platform for students, researchers and the wider community to engage directly with the night sky," an NIT-Srinagar spokesperson said. ALSO READ Tamil Nadu Expands Kamarajar Breakfast Scheme To Classes 6-8, Benefiting 15.30 Lakh Students Across... The centrepiece of the observatory is a 14-inch Celestron C14 EdgeHD Schmidt-Cassegrain telescope, equipped with a computerised equatorial mount and supported by specialised astronomical imaging equipment, he said. According to the spokesperson, the system includes planetary and cooled deep-sky cameras, LRGB filters, a 2.5x Barlow lens and high-speed imaging capabilities, allowing observations ranging from the Moon and planets to nebulae, star clusters and distant galaxies. The facility is being developed with scientific guidance and collaboration involving the Indian Institute of Astrophysics (IIA), Bengaluru, one of India's premier institutions dedicated to astronomy and astrophysics, he said. ALSO READ Maharashtra Forms AI Governance Committee To Transform Higher & Technical Education System Dr Niruj Mohan Ramanujam, Scientist F and Head of the Science Communication, Public Outreach and Education (SCOPE) Section at IIA, is associated with the initiative as an advisor and collaborator, he said. His expertise in astronomy education and large-scale public outreach adds an important dimension to the observatory's vision, the spokesperson said. "With the establishment of NSOAA, NIT-Srinagar will become the first National Institute of Technology to establish a dedicated campus-based observatory of this kind, providing students with access to advanced observational astronomy and astronomical imaging facilities," the spokesperson said. Speaking about the initiative, Professor and Head of the Department of Physics, NIT-Srinagar, Prince Ahmad Ganai, who is leading the project, said the observatory for Astronomy and Astrophysics is an effort to bring the excitement of observing and exploring the universe closer to our students. articles.title: Kandla-Thoothukudi to get weekly container service - DT Next
articles.content: CHENNAI: India’s first proposed Coastal Green Shipping Corridor connecting Gujarat’s Kandla on the west coast with VO Chidambaranar Port in Thoothukudi is set to get a dedicated weekly container service. The Indian Port Rail & Ropeway Corporation Ltd. (IPRCL) seeking a shipping company to operate it. The Kandla–Thoothukudi corridor was identified by the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways in 2025 as the first Coastal Green Shipping Corridor to be developed in partnership with the Shipping Corporation of India (SCI), Deendayal Port Authority and VOC Port Authority. The plan envisages greener maritime movement between the two ports and the development of green-fuel infrastructure along the route. The move to establish a regular container connection had already been discussed between VOC Port and SCI in June 2025. The discussions identified potential two-way cargo for the route, including raw The Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways identified it in 2025 as the first Coastal Green Shipping Corridor to be developed with SCI cotton and chemicals from Gujarat and solar panels, tyres and machinery spares from Tamil Nadu. The green shipping plan subsequently expanded beyond establishing a container connection. Under the latest IPRCL tender, the selected company will have to arrange and operate dedicated vessels between Kandla and Thoothukudi and back to Kandla. The service will require two vessels, each with a minimum capacity of 1,000 TEUs, to maintain a weekly frequency. The estimated round-trip voyage between the two ports is around 14 days. The service will initially be operated for six months and can be extended for up to two years, subject to cargo availability, operational requirements and satisfactory performance. IPRCL has estimated the project cost at Rs 150 crore. The selected company will be responsible for the operational side of the service, including arranging the vessels and crew, vessel scheduling and voyage management, bunker procurement, port agency coordination and payment of port dues and marine service charges. It will also have to coordinate cargo and terminal operations, including loading and unloading, manage vessel slots commercially and monitor cargo movement. The company will be expected to work with customers and stakeholders to attract bookings and facilitate cargo movement.
